question: On 17 and 18 October 2026, protests against the cost of living degenerated into coordinated acts of destruction in Italy and France. In Milan, Turin, Bologna and Bergamo, estimates put the ensuing damage at EUR 1.6 million. In Milan, almost half of the 50 or so people detained were minors.

In France, Limoges’ 19th-century town hall was largely destroyed, Marseille’s main bust of Marianne was toppled and Bordeaux’s Palais de la Bourse was wrecked. People who attack our cities’ history and heritage attack Europe’s foundations. A Europe-wide phenomenon calls for a European response, so that the 27 Member States do not act in isolation. In the light of the above: 1.
Will the Commission, in view of the Tjebbes and JY1 judgments, propose common guidelines on the withdrawal of citizenship, with the aim of addressing the current fragmentation?
What measures will it take, under Article 84 TFEU and together with Europol, to combat violent juvenile delinquency and the networks behind the destruction?
Will it activate EU instruments, in accordance with Article 167 TFEU, to protect and restore the historic heritage that has been damaged?

CJEU, Grand Chamber, 12 March 2019, Tjebbes and others, Case C-221/17, ECLI:EU:C:2019:189, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:62017CJ0221_RES; CJEU, Grand Chamber, 18 January 2022, JY, Case C-118/20, ECLI:EU:C:2022:34, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:62020CJ0118. 1
